recommendation_summary: Do now: swap in a new Cat6 patch cable, route it so it isn't pinched, and run normal calls to see whether the drops stop. If they keep happening, try a different router port, then check the computer's network port or adapter. The UniFi, managed-switch and Grafana setup is skipped and isn't offered now. Nothing needed is left out; the only unknown is whether the cable is really the cause, which the trial will show.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Dependable calls at the desk (you); future-proofing (you, prompted by your home-network group).
labels.Deleted: UniFi gateway, managed switches, Grafana dashboard. Two other devices on the same router keep their calls during a dropout, so the router and network aren't what's failing, and none of that gear touches the desk's own link.
labels.Bottleneck: The desk computer's link, most likely the old Ethernet cable squeezed through the tight grommet, which hasn't been ruled out.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing observed directly. You told me the drops happen only at the Ethernet desk, other devices stay connected during them, the cable is several years old and pinched in a grommet, and no other cable has been tried.

note: The fix is a bounded cable swap, the stack is named and rejected, and the Checked myself line uses only what the user said and admits nothing was observed directly.
